match.reason: Neither bank point teaches bank accounts, financial controls or record keeping for a business; both are about national balance of payments in economics.

draft.title: Bank accounts and record keeping
card: A business should open its own bank account and keep it separate from the owner's personal money. Mixing the two makes it hard to see what the business has earned and spent.
Financial controls are checks that protect the business's money. Examples are having two people approve large payments and matching bank statements to the records.
A business records its sales, its payments to suppliers and others, and the wages it pays staff. Each record should be accurate and kept up to date.
Accurate records are used to work out tax and to meet legal duties. They also show owners how the business is going, so they can decide on prices, stock and hiring.
draft.remember: Keep business money separate, check it, and record every sale, payment and wage accurately.

a.q: Tariq runs a bike repair shop in Geelong. He pays for his groceries from the shop's takings. What problem is this most likely to cause?
opts: It becomes hard to see what the shop really earned and spent
It stops the shop from paying wages to its staff
It means the shop no longer has to keep sales records
It lets the shop pay less tax without any checks
a.why: Mixing personal and business money blurs the business's real income and spending, which weakens tax records and decisions. It does not remove the need for sales records, which are still needed.
a.clue: Think about what a separate account makes clear.

b.q: Priya owns a bakery in Ballarat. Her records of sales and wages are accurate and current. Which is the best example of how she can use them for a decision?
opts: Check which products sell best before choosing what to bake
Pay herself from the till so the records stay simple
Keep one account for the bakery and her home bills
Ask staff to approve their own wage payments
b.why: Accurate sales records show what customers buy, so Priya can plan her baking from evidence. The other options mix money or weaken controls, which are the problems that good records and controls are meant to prevent.
b.clue: Which option uses the records to guide a choice about the business?

a.best: It becomes hard to see what the shop really earned and spent

b.best: Check which products sell best before choosing what to bake
